answer: Canyon Clock Admission: each identity must keep its request inter-arrival times inside a published envelope (no bursts, no dead air) and build a slow spiral of increasing uptime before earning full rate. Traffic shaping detects parallel identities sharing one machine’s clock: their micro-timing drifts. An attacker must rent distinct hosts and idle each one through the ramp, costing real compute hours per identity before any useful throughput—sybils pay wall-clock time, not fees, so a grove of fakes grows linearly expensive.
